Since target equals pose, segment_free will check segment from pose to same point? segment_free uses check_path([p,q]) where p==q, length zero, but check_path requires at least two points and will compute samples with count = max(1, int(ceil(0/...))) => 1 sample? Since target is same as robot, projected distance is zero, reason "behind" or "too_near"? In guard_target, they compute projected = _base_loop_projection(path, requested, robot["s"]). If requested same as robot, distance maybe 0, ahead = projected["s"] - robot["s"] = 0. Then reason = "too_near" if ahead < target_min_ahead_m (0.3). So reason = "too_near". Then they try fallback: _base_loop_forward_target(path, pose, robot). That returns forward target if remaining >= target_min_ahead_m. So min_gap_map 0.21 indicates map clearance is low (close to obstacle). That's why stop is chosen.

So if min_gap_map = 0.21, that means distance to object is 0.21, less than robot half width 0.25? Wait map_clearance returns distance to object from point. For body perimeter points, they compute min distance. So if min_gap_map 0.21, robot is within 0.21 m of obstacle, i.e., less than half width. That's unsafe. So the path is too close.

So min_gap_map is (distance to object) - 0.25. So if min_gap_map = 0.35, then distance to object = 0.6. So robot center is 0.6 away, good. So path is safe.

But during motion, map gaps computed without subtracting half width, margin 0.2. So if distance to object is 0.6, min_gap_map = 0.6, not 0.21. So why we see 0.21? Possibly because the robot is at a point not on the path, maybe due to target being robot itself, causing no forward movement, so robot stays near start where path maybe close to wall. Actually base loop: requested = lookahead_target(...); then target = _base_loop_pair(requested,...). So lookahead_target must return a pair. If we return None, _base_loop_pair will raise error. So we must return a valid point. The current approach returns robot position, causing stop. Better to return a point slightly ahead (e.g., robot position + 0.3 m forward) to satisfy forward range, so guard will accept it and follow. So modify lookahead_target to compute forward target using base's helper _base_loop_forward_target directly and if None, maybe return a point 0.3 m ahead along robot heading. That would avoid repeated stop.
